title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Picture 25's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$004B, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0027, channel 2's script at +$0031 and channel 3's script at +$0041.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 2, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 6, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 5. One pass takes 18 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 10, frame 3 then 5, frame 3 then 25. One pass takes 40 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 3, frame 4 then 5, frame 4 then 15, frame 4 then 9, frame 4 then 7. One pass takes 39 steps.

Channel 3's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 5, frame 5 then 3, frame 5 then 3. One pass takes 11 steps.

Picture 25's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $05 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 22 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 25, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 25, named by channel 1's entry 1, channel 2's entry 1 and channel 3's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 3 of picture 25, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in column 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 25, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 2, 3, 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 19 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 57 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 7 to 11. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 25, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 3's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 12 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 1 to 3. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 25's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,102nd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
